transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-03-05 15:00 PST
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lina Chen (Redwood SE), Jordan Blake (AtlasCare CTO), Aisha Khan (AtlasCare Head of ML), Marcus Lee (AtlasCare Procurement)

Summary:
Quick scoping for a 3-month pilot: success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan, and commercial guardrails (credits, pilot terms, path to procurement/contracting). Focus on latency SLOs, throughput needs, and security/KMS questions.

Topics:
- Success criteria & acceptance tests
- Workload sizing (tokens/month, QPS, concurrency)
- Benchmark types and metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, cold vs warm start)
- Pilot commercial guardrails: credits, duration, support, procurement path
- Security/compliance (SOC2, KMS, VPC peering)

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Samir from Redwood, i have Lina from our SE team as well. quick intro round?
[00:07] Jordan: Jordan here, CTO at AtlasCare, i'll be owning infra/ops side.
[00:11] Aisha: Aisha, head of ML, i'll own the bench marks and model quality checks.
[00:15] Marcus: Marcus from procurement, i'll handle contracting and PO questions.
[00:20] Lina: great thanks — high level agenda: align on success criteria, get sizing, agree benchmark plan and then commercial guardrails for the pilot.

[03:05] Samir: to set expectations on the pilot — typical Redwood pilot is 8–12 weeks but we do a 12 week path often broken into a 4 week initial benchmark + 8 week pilot. For commercial guardrails we offer credits, usually a credit draw model mapped to token usage and endpoints. For enterprise procurement we can support a PO, SOW, and then a path to a term contract.
[03:37] Jordan: sounds fine, our timeline is tight — want production proof within Q2. What do you need from us to size this?
[03:50] Lina: best is sample traces: token histogram (per request token counts), requests per minute over 30 days, concurrency peaks. If you can share a few representative prompt sets we can run realistic benchmarks.
[04:12] Aisha: we can provide a 30 day trace and a few flagged prompts. rough numbers — currently our chat workload averages 200 tokens per response, 30k requests/day, peaks at ~120 QPS during batch windows.
[04:30] Samir: ok that maps to about 200M tokens/month — do you expect growth?
[04:35] Aisha: yes expect 2x growth over 6 months if pilot becomes prod.

[06:00] Lina: benchmark plan we recommend: 1) cold start latency (first request after idle), 2) steady-state throughput with your concurrency and batching settings, 3) 99th percentile latency under realistic load, 4) cost per 1M tokens simulated. we'll run both hosted and a dedicated config if you want to compare.
[06:35] Jordan: we care about 99p latency — target is <700ms for conversational flows, ideally p95 < 300ms.
[06:44] Samir: that's doable for many model+quant combos; we'll surface a matrix: hosted low-cost variant vs dedicated-reserved with better tail latency.

[08:10] Aisha: what models are you thinking? we want open model parity — maybe Llama-3 8B variants, and a quantized 4-bit variant for cost checks.
[08:22] Lina: yes we can run Llama-3 family, quantized int8/int4, and a Redwood-verified smaller model. note: quantization changes quality a bit — we'll include quality checks against your eval set.

[11:00] Samir: commercial guardrails conversation: typical pilot credit structure is 3 months of credits e.g. $10–25k depending on throughput needs. credits cover usage (tokens + inference runtime) and we can cap spend. if you need dedicated capacity there's a deposit or reserved commit for the pilot.
[11:28] Marcus: procurement question — do you require a contract prior to spinning up pilot or can we do it under an intake form/PO?
[11:38] Samir: we do a lightweight pilot SOW and an intake PO works for many customers; for dedicated or larger pilots we often do a short-term MSA addendum or simple pilot contract. we can adapt to your procurement policy — please share your contracting template.

[13:50] Jordan: about security — we need SOC2 evidence, audit logs, RBAC, SSO/SAML, KMS integration for keys. and data residency for EU customers.
[14:05] Lina: we have a security deck (SOC2, ISO statements), audit logs + token-level tracing in Redwood Console, and KMS/HSM integration for private deployments. for pilots we can do VPC peering or a private deployment depending on your sensitivity. we'll share the security-deck.pdf.
[14:28] Aisha: for the benchmark we also want to run a data residency test — i.e., route inference via EU region.

[17:10] Samir: pricing guardrails — two common approaches: 1) flat credit bucket (we give you $X credits and you consume until exhausted) or 2) capped usage profile (we set a QPS/throughput cap and alert if exceeded). credits approach is simplest.
[17:40] Marcus: if we go credit model, what's the refund/rollover policy if we don't use it all?
[17:48] Samir: pilots generally do not auto-refund; unused credit can be applied to initial invoice for production if we move forward within 90 days, we can add flexible terms in the SOW.

[20:00] Lina: success criteria suggestions: 1) performance: meet p95/p99 latency SLOs under your peak concurrency; 2) cost: per-1M-token cost within target threshold compared to your budget; 3) quality: model responses pass your evals with <5% regression; 4) operational: ability to run in your VPC or via private deployment if required.
[20:38] Aisha: quality checks — we'll run an eval set of ~2k prompts and check for hallucination/accuracy metrics; acceptable regression window is strict — <2% drop vs current baseline.

[23:12] Samir: benchmark logistics: we'll need sample prompts, a small eval harness (we can share a Jupyter harness), and preferred models. Lina will coordinate the staging run; expect first benchmark report within 7–10 business days after we get traces.
[23:30] Lina: yes i'll run a warm vs cold start, concurrency sweep (1, 4, 8, 16), and microbench for KV cache effectiveness on conversation workloads.

[26:00] Jordan: what about fallback/resilience? how do you handle model fallbacks if capacity is constrained?
[26:12] Samir: smart routing — we can route to a compatible model variant (lower cost or smaller size) automatically as fallback, and we have canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies in Redwood Console. we'll surface expected quality deltas.

[29:45] Marcus: timeline for procurement end to end? if pilot goes well we need enterprise terms by end of Q2.
[29:55] Samir: typical path: pilot sign-off -> PO for production capacity or reserved commit -> SOW/MSA negotiation (2–4 weeks depending on redlines) -> onboarding. we can compress this if procurement team is responsive.

[33:10] Aisha: on sizing again — if we double to 400M tokens/mo what changes for latency/cost?
[33:20] Lina: cost scales linearly with token consumption but latency tail can be improved with dedicated pools. we'd likely recommend a dedicated reserved GPU pool if you're steady at 400M/mo to hit stronger tail latency with sustained throughput.

[35:50] Samir: on the pilot credits number — based on your 200M tokens/mo profile a reasonable pilot credit bucket for a 6–8 week active test is $12,000–18,000 to cover multiple model runs and iterations; we can mark a hard cap and provide alerts.
[36:10] Marcus: ok that range is helpful. we need to see exact line items to get internal approval.

[40:00] Lina: risks and mitigations: 1) quality regression on quantized models — mitigate with eval sets and hold-out checks; 2) procurement delays — we can start staging benchmarks without PO under limited trial credits; 3) data residency — mitigate via EU region or private deployment.

[44:30] Samir: recap/next steps: Samir to send pilot_pricing.xlsx with credit tiers and sample SOW; Lina to share security deck and kick off staging benchmark once AtlasCare sends sample traces; Aisha to provide traces and eval prompts; Marcus to share procurement template.
[45:05] Jordan: agreed, we'll aim to get traces and procurement template by next week.
[45:20] Aisha: i'll drop the 30-day trace into the shared drive today.
[45:30] Marcus: i'll review the pricing spreadsheet when you send it.
[46:00] Samir: great thanks everyone — we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark kickoff and share artifacts.
[46:18] Jordan: thanks all.

End of transcript.

References/Artifacts mentioned:
- pilot_pricing.xlsx (Samir)
- security-deck.pdf (Lina)
- Jupyter eval harness (Lina)
- pilot SOW template (Legal)

POC Acceptance criteria (not exhaustive):
- p95 latency < 300ms and p99 < 700ms on conversational flows at peak concurrency (or clearly documented tradeoff),
- <2% quality regression on AtlasCare eval set,
- Benchmarks show cost within pilot credit bucket,
- Security docs reviewed: SOC2 evidence + KMS plan agreed,
- Procurement path agreed (PO or SOW) and initial pilot credits provisioned.
